**Why these work:** If $P(x)=c$, then for $\omega(n)>2023^{2023}$ we have $\omega(n)\ge 2023^{2023}+1\ge\omega(c)=\omega(P(n))$. If $P(x)=x^k$, then $\omega(P(n))=\omega(n^k)=\omega(n)$.

**Why nothing else works:** Let $T=2023^{2023}$. Suppose $P$ is non-constant and not of the form $x^k$. Write $P(x)=x^kQ(x)$ with $k\ge 0$, $Q(0)\ne 0$, and $Q$ non-constant. By Schur's theorem there are infinitely many primes $q$ for which $q\mid Q(a_q)$ with $q\nmid a_q$. Pick $r\ge 1$ such primes $q_1,\dots,q_r$ and $m>T$ distinct primes $p_1,\dots,p_m$ disjoint from them. By CRT choose $n$ with $n\equiv 0\pmod{p_1\cdots p_m}$ and $n\equiv a_i\pmod{q_i}$. By Dirichlet, we may take $n=p_1\cdots p_m\cdot\ell$ with $\ell$ a new prime, so $\omega(n)=m+1>T$. Then $q_i\mid Q(n)$ and $q_i\nmid n$, giving $\omega(P(n))\ge\omega(n)+r>\omega(n)$, contradiction.

For a monomial $P(x)=cx^k$ with $k\ge 1$ and $c>1$, pick $n$ coprime to $c$ having $>T$ prime factors; then $\omega(P(n))=\omega(c)+\omega(n)>\omega(n)$, impossible. Hence $c=1$.
